Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you draft a short email about the shared studio access list? address it to Saskia, not Ellis. Saskia is coordinating the list this month and asked me to send name changes straight to her. Jo Park has joined our ceramics studio and needs access added; their first booked session is Thursday, 12 June, from 6 to 8 p.m. The list currently has Jo's name misspelled as Joe Park in a note, but Jo hasn't been added to the actual access list yet. Please ask Saskia to add Jo Park and use the spelling Jo, not Joe. Don't ask her to remove anyone else, and don't imply the change is already done. Mention that I'll be at the front desk at 5:45 to collect the studio key, so the update needs to be in place before then. The weekly room booking calendar already includes Jo's booking, so don't ask to change it. Keep the note friendly and straightforward, and make it clear the request is for this one person's access only. I only need a message about this individual request, not an announcement to all studio members. No need to explain the studio rules or add a subject line. Could you keep the timing and names clear and make it sound like something I'd actually send?", "output": "Draft a short, friendly, straightforward email about the shared studio access list, addressed to Saskia, not Ellis. Saskia is coordinating the list this month and asked me to send name changes directly to her. Jo Park has joined our ceramics studio and needs to be added to the access list for their first booked session on Thursday, 12 June, from 6 to 8 p.m. A note currently misspells Jo's name as Joe Park, but Jo has not yet been added to the actual access list. Ask Saskia to add Jo Park, using the spelling Jo, not Joe. Do not ask her to remove anyone else or imply that the change has already been made. Mention that I will be at the front desk at 5:45 to collect the studio key, so the access-list update is needed before then. Jo's booking is already on the weekly room booking calendar, so do not request a calendar change. Keep the request limited to Jo's access; write a message about this individual request, not an announcement to studio members. There is no need to explain the studio rules or include a subject line. Make the names and timing clear, and make the email sound like something I would actually send."}]
